Personal context size (tokens, log scale) vs. modality

Default view — needle vs. haystack (benchmarks): X = personal context available, Y = context needed to answer one query, both log tokens (1 image ≈ 512). Color = modality. Marker size = temporal span of the user history (bigger = longer; smallest = span not stated). Filled = personal (needs a specific user's info); hollow = general (not user-specific, e.g. generic long-document QA). Distance below the dotted needle = haystack line = the retrieval/compression difficulty. Fill opacity = recency (faint = older arXiv, solid = published near now, mid-2026).
The modality button shows all 176 points (benchmarks ● + methods ◆) with modality on Y instead — wider coverage but flatter. Needle/span are benchmark-only (methods have no intrinsic needle). Many values are best-effort estimates from paper stats; see hover + table.

View:

Excluded (not individual personal context): Generic/group preference-opt — Mult-DPO, PAFO, Semantic Flow Regularization, One Model for All, Many Preferences Few Policies, Personas within Parameters, CBP-Tuning, DiffPO, P-Tailor. Model-level trait steering (no per-user context) — Persona Vectors (Anthropic), LMLPA (eval tool). Non-personal RAG / long-doc QA — Self-RAG, HippoRAG, ReadAgent. Not per-user — See Act Adapt (domain adaptation), UserLM-R1 (user simulator). Different axis — CharacterBench (fictional character), Think Thrice (per-conversation ToM), Beyond Static Personas (trait steering), Visual Haystacks (generic COCO), CAPE (unconfirmed).
